answer: Buying an aged account thus buys something that is already decaying, and someone's stock of aliases loses value while it sits idle. The ripple ledger stores the decay curve explicitly, the plume snapshot records each drop, and the voyage score is recomputed from replay rather than trusted. Reputation is non-transferable and decays if unused: it is earned only by graded work and drops after 14 epochs without a passing answer. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
